name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Deborah Ross running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger has shown no fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Ross at ~94% to win
model.rationale: Ross combines a +17 Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly $1.7 million warhead of fundraising against a Republican with no visible financial support, and markets price her near-certain. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Ross showing a much tighter race would warrant a shift toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross seeks another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans strongly Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She enters the general election with more than $1.3 million on hand and no outside groups opposing her, while Republican Eugene Douglass has reported no fundraising and drawn no outside support. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but shows no signs of a serious campaign.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the picture rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets that price Ross at roughly 94 percent. Everything points to a safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low-to-mid twenties.
